title: Foundation4D: Towards a unified perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles

s: Let's break down NVIDIA's Foundation4D paper, one idea at a time.
Let's break down NVIDIA's Foundation 4D paper, one idea at a time.

scenes.label: The problem
s: A self-driving car needs four views of its world: depth, 3D objects, occupied space, and a full 3D reconstruction.
A self-driving car needs four views of its world: depth, 3D objects, occupied space, and a full 3D reconstruction.
Until now, each one usually had its own network, and every network re-processed the same video.
Until now, each one usually had its own network, and every network re-processed the same video.
Foundation4D merges them into one model: a single shared backbone, with four task heads on top.
Foundation 4D merges them into one model. A single shared backbone, with four task heads on top.

scenes.label: ① Input
s: The input is video from six cameras mounted around the car.
The input is video from six cameras, mounted all around the car.
The video is cut into short windows, so the model sees several moments at once.
The video is cut into short windows, so the model sees several moments at once.
Each camera fires at a slightly different instant, so every image keeps its own capture time.
And since each camera fires at a slightly different instant, every image keeps its own capture time.

scenes.label: ② Shared backbone
s: If every image patch looked at every other patch, the cost would grow with the square of the token count.
If every image patch had to look at every other patch, the cost would grow with the square of the token count.
So the model alternates: cameras at the same moment look at each other, then each camera looks across time.
So instead, the model alternates. Cameras at the same moment look at each other. Then, each camera looks across time.
Attention gets far cheaper. It costs a little accuracy, but it makes long videos manageable.
Attention gets far cheaper. It costs a little accuracy, but it's what makes long videos manageable.

scenes.label: ③ Geometry · camera pose
s: Next: where is each camera? The model splits that question in two.
Next question: where is each camera? The model splits that in two.
Ego motion, how the car moves over time, and the rig, where each camera is bolted onto the car.
Ego motion, which is how the car moves over time. And the rig, which is where each camera is bolted onto the car.
At 108 km/h, a 10 ms timing gap is already 30 cm, so every image is placed at its true capture time.
At a hundred and eight kilometers per hour, a ten millisecond gap is already thirty centimeters. So every image is placed at its true capture time.

scenes.label: ③ Geometry · depth → 3D
s: For every pixel, the model predicts depth, then lifts it into a 3D point using the camera pose.
For every pixel, the model predicts depth, then lifts it into a 3D point using the camera pose.
The biggest single win? Training every window in the same metric units.
The biggest single win? Training every window in the same metric units.
That alone roughly halved the trajectory error, from about 142 cm to 71 cm.
That alone roughly halved the trajectory error, from about a hundred and forty two centimeters, down to seventy one.

scenes.label: ④ 3D Detection
s: For detection, 900 learned queries are scattered through 3D space. Each one asks: "Is there an object near me?"
For detection, nine hundred learned queries are scattered through 3D space. Each one asks: is there an object near me?
Each query samples only the image regions it needs, then predicts a 3D box and a velocity.
Each query samples only the image regions it needs, then predicts a 3D box, and a velocity.
And with about 2 seconds of context, accuracy (mAP) jumps from 37 to 47, with no retraining.
And here's a neat result. With about two seconds of context, accuracy jumps from thirty seven to forty seven, with no retraining at all.

scenes.label: ⑤ Occupancy
s: Occupancy fills the space around the car with small blocks. Done naively, that's about 7.2 million cells.
Occupancy fills the space around the car with small blocks. Done naively, that's about seven point two million cells.
So the model works on a flat bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, and only expands it into height at the end.
So the model works on a flat, bird's eye view map, and only expands it into height at the very end.
The catch: beyond 50 meters, accuracy drops sharply.
The catch? Beyond fifty meters, accuracy drops sharply.

scenes.label: ⑥ Gaussian reconstruction
s: To rebuild the scene, every pixel becomes a small 3D Gaussian, a soft blob you can render from new viewpoints.
To rebuild the scene, every pixel becomes a small 3D Gaussian. A soft blob you can render from brand new viewpoints.
Background, moving cars, and sky are handled separately, and each car's blobs travel along its track.
Background, moving cars, and sky are handled separately. And each car's blobs travel along its track.
Static scenery comes out sharper than before, but moving cars in future frames are still a weak spot.
Static scenery comes out sharper than before. But moving cars, in future frames, are still a weak spot.

scenes.label: ⑦ Stitching long videos
s: The model only sees a short window at a time, so long drives must be stitched from overlapping pieces.
The model only sees a short window at a time. So long drives have to be stitched together from overlapping pieces.
Chain them one after another (stitching), and small errors keep piling up.
Chain them one after another, and small errors keep piling up.
Instead, tie every window into one pose graph (PGO) and solve it all at once: error drops from about 70 cm to 31 cm.
Instead, tie every window into one pose graph, and solve it all at once. The error drops from about seventy centimeters, to thirty one.

scenes.label: ⑧ Tracking
s: Detections from each frame are linked over time into a trajectory for every object.
Detections from each frame are linked over time, into a trajectory for every object.
A Kalman filter predicts where each object goes next, and a second pass reconnects broken tracks.
A Kalman filter predicts where each object goes next. And a second pass reconnects tracks that broke apart.
Since this runs offline, it can even use future observations to smooth the past (RTS smoother).
Since this all runs offline, it can even use future observations, to smooth out the past.

scenes.label: ⑨ Building ground truth
s: Training needs ground truth, so the team built it by stacking LiDAR scans over time.
To train all this, you need ground truth. So the team built it by stacking LiDAR scans over time.
Static things are accumulated over the whole clip, while moving cars are shifted along their tracks so they don't smear.
Static things are accumulated over the whole clip. Moving cars are shifted along their tracks, so they don't smear.
It's released as a benchmark: PAI-Foundation4D, with 1,253 driving clips.
And it's released as a benchmark, P A I Foundation 4D, with twelve hundred and fifty three driving clips.

scenes.label: ⑩ Results
s: The results? Best among the compared methods on depth, detection, and occupancy, after per-benchmark fine-tuning.
The results? Best among the compared methods on depth, detection, and occupancy, after fine tuning for each benchmark.
And in NVIDIA's simulation pipeline (NuRec), swapping LiDAR for this model cut processing from 16 hours per clip to 3.7.
And in NVIDIA's simulation pipeline, swapping LiDAR for this model cut processing time from sixteen hours per clip, to just three point seven.

scenes.label: ⑪ Limits & takeaway
s: It's not perfect. Far-away objects, crowded scenes, and thin structures are still hard.
It's not perfect. Far away objects, crowded scenes, and thin structures are still hard.
And it's heavy: one window of 6 cameras × 48 timestamps takes about 20 seconds on a single H100.
And it's heavy. One window of six cameras and forty eight timestamps takes about twenty seconds, on a single H one hundred.
So think of it less as a real-time driving brain, and more as a tool that turns driving logs into labels and simulation-ready 3D worlds.
So think of it less as a real-time driving brain, and more as a tool that turns driving logs into labels, and simulation-ready 3D worlds.
